b1-centroamerica-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Somoza Dynasty
b1-centroamerica-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg have watched a documentary about Nicaragua, and she asks how long the Somoza family ruled.
b1-centroamerica-01.prompt: Tell Meg how long the Somoza family had ruled when the regime fell.
cues: Say how long the family had ruled
b1-centroamerica-01.target: Cuando cayó Somoza, la familia había gobernado más de cuarenta años.
b1-centroamerica-01.english: When Somoza fell, the family had ruled for more than forty years.
b1-centroamerica-01.canDo: I can say how long the Somoza family had ruled Nicaragua when the regime fell.

b1-centroamerica-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Archbishop Romero
b1-centroamerica-02.scenario: You are Meg. You read about El Salvador for a class, and Carlos asks what happened to Archbishop Romero.
b1-centroamerica-02.prompt: Tell Carlos when and how Romero was killed.
cues: Say on which date he was killed
Say what he was doing at that moment
b1-centroamerica-02.target: Romero fue asesinado el 24 de marzo de 1980, mientras celebraba misa.
b1-centroamerica-02.english: Romero was killed on 24 March 1980, while he was saying Mass.
b1-centroamerica-02.canDo: I can say when and how Archbishop Romero was killed, using cuando and mientras.

b1-centroamerica-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Guatemalan Commission
b1-centroamerica-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a presentation on Guatemala, and she asks what the commission counted.
b1-centroamerica-03.prompt: Tell Meg what the commission counted and when it presented its report.
cues: Mention the commission and when its report came out
Say how many dead or disappeared people it counted
b1-centroamerica-03.target: La CEH, que presentó su informe en 1999, contó más de 200.000 muertos o desaparecidos.
b1-centroamerica-03.english: The CEH, which presented its report in 1999, counted more than 200,000 dead or disappeared people.
b1-centroamerica-03.canDo: I can describe the Guatemalan conflict and what the commission found, with relative clauses.

b1-centroamerica-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The United States and the Contras
b1-centroamerica-04.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have just seen an exhibition about the Cold War, and he asks what Congress did about the Contras.
b1-centroamerica-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what the United States did for the Contras and what Congress did.
cues: Say that the United States helped the Contras
Contrast this with what Congress did
b1-centroamerica-04.target: Estados Unidos ayudó a los contras. Sin embargo, el Congreso limitó esa ayuda.
b1-centroamerica-04.english: The United States helped the Contras. However, Congress limited that aid.
b1-centroamerica-04.canDo: I can explain what the United States did in Central America and what its critics said.

b1-centroamerica-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Road to Peace
b1-centroamerica-05.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are putting together a timeline for a class, and she asks how the peace process went.
b1-centroamerica-05.prompt: Tell Meg the main steps of the peace process in order.
cues: Say what the presidents signed first
Say what happened in Nicaragua next
Say how it ended in Guatemala
b1-centroamerica-05.target: Primero, los presidentes firmaron Esquipulas II en 1987. Luego, Violeta Chamorro ganó las elecciones de Nicaragua en 1990. Al final, Guatemala firmó la paz en 1996.
b1-centroamerica-05.english: First, the presidents signed Esquipulas II in 1987. Then Violeta Chamorro won the elections in Nicaragua in 1990. In the end, Guatemala signed peace in 1996.
b1-centroamerica-05.canDo: I can put the steps of the peace process in order with primero, luego, después and al final.

b1-centroamerica-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Nicaragua in Review
b1-centroamerica-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are going over your notes on Central America for a class, and he asks what you remember about Nicaragua.
b1-centroamerica-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what the Somoza family had done before the Sandinistas took power.
cues: Say when the Sandinistas took power
Say how long the family had already ruled
b1-centroamerica-consolidation.target: Cuando los sandinistas tomaron el poder, los Somoza ya habían gobernado más de cuarenta años.
b1-centroamerica-consolidation.english: When the Sandinistas took power, the Somozas had already ruled for more than forty years.
b1-centroamerica-consolidation.canDo: I can use the pluperfect to say what had already happened in Nicaragua before 1979.
